summary: Day 1 of the 5-session grading window went mildly against the risk-on call: the SPY benchmark value fell from 589.21 to 587.04 (about -0.37%), putting SPY near 750, still about 3% above the 727.98 200-day line, so the regime holds and nothing in the stance's watch list has tripped. The weak spot was rates, not equities. The PM's reasoning cites a hot October CPI, and the held bond sleeves fell with equities (IEF -0.83%, BND -0.71% on the day). That cuts against my 'bonds as ballast' view on an inflation day. Equity damage was modest and mixed (IDXX -1.42%, DPZ -1.23%, VOO -0.29%, VTI -0.17%, VNQ -0.23%; VRSN +2.01%, MSCI +1.61%). The account lost about -0.17% (-1.08 on 623.40).
broken_theses: Bonds as ballast (asset_class_view.bonds_gold): on a CPI-driven down day the bond ETFs fell with equities instead of offsetting them (IEF -0.83%, BND -0.71% vs VOO -0.29%). It is one day, but it is the exact case the hedge is meant to cover, and TLT and IEF were already below their 200-day averages (-1.02%, -0.40%) this morning, so the trend never confirmed.
update: Keep risk-on at low confidence for now. 'Held up' is provisional: one of five sessions is in, and SPY needs about +1.4% over the next four to make the call right. The regime cushion (about 3%) and the absence of credit or volatility stress are unchanged, but this packet has no today's reading for RSP, HYG or VIXY, so breadth and credit cannot be re-confirmed until tomorrow's inputs. Next run: (1) treat the CPI print as a live rates shock and check whether TLT has slipped further below its 200-day (more than 3% below also touches the VNQ invalidation clause), and if so stop calling Treasuries ballast and prefer cash-like BND/SHY over IEF/TLT; (2) if HYG loses its 200-day or VIXY jumps on the 5-day, move to neutral or risk-off; (3) favor-Real-Estate should be re-checked, since REITs are rate-sensitive into hike odds even though VNQ held up today (-0.23%). Lessons L1 to L5 are proposer and PM process lessons and none applies to this review. My record (0.60) still only ties the always-neutral baseline (0.60).
